Save your money and look for a better fitness app.

reviews.author: ThornHona
reviews.title: disappointed, hidden charges and app quality has gone downhill
reviews.content: This app has become a money grab. I have used this app for a long time, but the current version is extremely disappointing. The biggest issue is the subscription trap. I signed up for a trial expecting a trial experience, but I was charged afterward without a clear enough reminder. I have reported this to Apple because this kind of payment experience is not acceptable. What makes it worse is that the app itself is getting worse every year. The workouts are outdated, repetitive, and lack creativity. It feels like the team is recycling old content instead of creating new and useful fitness programs. For a paid fitness app, the lack of fresh content is unacceptable. I also noticed that critical reviews disappear, which makes me question how much the company values honest user feedback. This app used to have potential, but now it feels like the priority is getting subscriptions rather than delivering a quality fitness experience. Save your money and look for a better fitness app.

versions.name: Restore access to previously free workouts
versions.rationale: F-01 is a high-confidence, high-frequency P1 issue where long-time users are locked out of core workouts by a paywall. It directly blocks usability and subscription conversion, so it must be addressed first.

versions.name: Fix misleading billing and subscription charges
versions.rationale: F-02 is P0 severity but low confidence and lower support; it still represents a critical trust and conversion risk. It is scheduled after validating evidence and after the access blocker is resolved.

versions.name: Reduce workout disruptions from ads and AI quality decline
versions.rationale: F-04 and F-05 are P2 issues with lower support counts. They affect workout usability but are less urgent; they can be bundled as a usability improvement release after critical subscription and access issues.

requirements.title: Restore free access to previously free workouts
requirements.problem: Long-time users report that previously free workouts and features are locked behind a mandatory subscription, making the app unusable without payment.
requirements.user_need: As a long-time user, I want to access the workouts I used for free so that I can continue my fitness routine without being forced to pay.
requirements.description: Restore access to core workouts that were free before the subscription paywall was introduced. Existing users should be grandfathered in and not see a paywall for content they already accessed.
acceptance_criteria: Existing users who previously accessed free workouts can access the same workout collection without being prompted to subscribe.
No paywall appears for core workout content that was free in the app version before the subscription introduction.
New users continue to see subscription prompts only for premium features, not for the previously free core workouts.

requirements.title: Prevent misleading billing and unauthorized subscription charges
requirements.problem: Users report unauthorized or unexpected charges, confusing pricing, and inability to cancel trials before being charged.
requirements.user_need: As a user evaluating a subscription, I want clear pricing and easy cancellation so that I am not charged unexpectedly.
requirements.description: Improve billing transparency and cancellation flows. Ensure all subscription terms and charges are clearly disclosed before purchase and that users can cancel without being charged after trial.
acceptance_criteria: Before any charge, the app displays the exact price, currency, billing frequency, and trial end date.
Users can cancel a trial or subscription directly from the app and receive confirmation.
No charges occur after a user cancels before the trial end date.
System logs show no billing events for users who completed cancellation before the charge date.
assumptions: Finding is based on 4 reviews with low confidence; the true frequency of billing issues may be higher or lower and requires further validation through support tickets and payment logs.

requirements.title: Make ads dismissible and non-disruptive
requirements.problem: Ads are impossible to exit after watching, or cause the app to close and open external websites unexpectedly during workouts.
requirements.user_need: As a user in a workout, I want ads that I can close easily and that do not interrupt my session, so I can focus on exercising.
requirements.description: Redesign ad experience to ensure ads have close controls, do not auto-redirect, and do not crash the app during workouts.
acceptance_criteria: Every ad overlay includes a visible close button that dismisses the ad with one tap.
The app does not automatically open external websites or app store pages after an ad is shown or dismissed.
No app crash or forced close occurs during ad display or dismissal.
Ads do not interrupt active workout sessions unless intentionally triggered by the user.
assumptions: Finding has low confidence with 3 supporting reviews; ad behavior may vary by ad network and device, requiring additional testing logs.

requirements.title: Restore content quality and original workout content
requirements.problem: Long-time users feel the app has gotten worse over time, citing AI-generated workouts and avatars replacing original content, and updates that reduce quality.
requirements.user_need: As a long-time user, I want access to the original, human-created workouts and not have AI content replace what I already liked, so the app remains useful to me.
requirements.description: Provide access to original workout content and ensure AI-generated content is clearly labeled and does not replace existing content without user opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: Original workout library available before the AI update is still accessible.
AI-generated workouts are labeled as AI and are optional additions, not replacements for existing workouts.
User can switch between AI-generated and original content in settings.
Following the update, user crash-free session rate and workout completion rate remain at or above pre-update baseline.
assumptions: Finding has medium confidence; quality perceptions are subjective, and some decline may be due to changing user expectations. Further user testing may be needed to define objective quality metrics.

App updated to latest version containing the fix.

Navigate to the workout library.
Attempt to open a workout that was previously accessed for free.
Observe if any paywall or subscription prompt appears.
expected_results: The workout opens and plays without any paywall or subscription prompt.
The user can access the full workout content exactly as before the paywall was introduced.

steps: Open the app and navigate to the workout categories/list.
Identify core workouts that were previously free.
Attempt to start one of those core workouts without a subscription.
expected_results: The core workout starts or plays without requiring a subscription.
No paywall overlay appears; any upsell is non-blocking and does not prevent access to the core workout.

New user account with no prior history.

Browse workouts and attempt to access a core workout that was previously free.
Observe any prompts.

Observe any prompts.
expected_results: The previously free core workout is accessible without any subscription prompt.

Review all text and disclosures on the screen.
Note the displayed price, currency, billing frequency, and trial end date.
expected_results: The screen explicitly shows the exact numeric price, currency symbol (e.g., $39.99 USD), billing frequency (e.g., yearly), and exact trial end date and time.
All required billing details are visible before user confirms purchase.

test_cases.title: Verify user can cancel trial/subscription directly from app and receive confirmation

User is logged into the app.

Find the cancellation option.
Initiate cancellation and confirm.
Observe the confirmation message and subscription status change.

User receives a clear confirmation message indicating the subscription is cancelled and no further charges will occur.
Subscription status changes to cancelled immediately.

Allow the ad to complete or close it.
Observe if any external website or app store page opens automatically.

If the ad is closed, no redirect occurs.
If the ad is watched to completion, no auto-redirect occurs.

requirements.user_need: As a user evaluating a subscription, I want clear pricing and easy cancellation so that I am not charged unexpectedly.
requirements.description: Improve billing transparency and cancellation flows. Ensure all subscription terms and charges are clearly disclosed before purchase and that users can cancel without being charged after trial.
acceptance_criteria: Before any charge, the app displays the exact price, currency, billing frequency, and trial end date.
Users can cancel a trial or subscription directly from the app and receive confirmation.
No charges occur after a user cancels before the trial end date.
System logs show no billing events for users who completed cancellation before the charge date.
assumptions: Finding is based on 4 reviews with low confidence; the true frequency of billing issues may be higher or lower and requires further validation through support tickets and payment logs.

requirements.title: Make ads dismissible and non-disruptive
requirements.problem: Ads are impossible to exit after watching, or cause the app to close and open external websites unexpectedly during workouts.
requirements.user_need: As a user in a workout, I want ads that I can close easily and that do not interrupt my session, so I can focus on exercising.
requirements.description: Redesign ad experience to ensure ads have close controls, do not auto-redirect, and do not crash the app during workouts.
acceptance_criteria: Every ad overlay includes a visible close button that dismisses the ad with one tap.
The app does not automatically open external websites or app store pages after an ad is shown or dismissed.
No app crash or forced close occurs during ad display or dismissal.
Ads do not interrupt active workout sessions unless intentionally triggered by the user.
assumptions: Finding has low confidence with 3 supporting reviews; ad behavior may vary by ad network and device, requiring additional testing logs.

requirements.title: Restore content quality and original workout content
requirements.problem: Long-time users feel the app has gotten worse over time, citing AI-generated workouts and avatars replacing original content, and updates that reduce quality.
requirements.user_need: As a long-time user, I want access to the original, human-created workouts and not have AI content replace what I already liked, so the app remains useful to me.
requirements.description: Provide access to original workout content and ensure AI-generated content is clearly labeled and does not replace existing content without user opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: Original workout library available before the AI update is still accessible.
AI-generated workouts are labeled as AI and are optional additions, not replacements for existing workouts.
User can switch between AI-generated and original content in settings.
Following the update, user crash-free session rate and workout completion rate remain at or above pre-update baseline.
assumptions: Finding has medium confidence; quality perceptions are subjective, and some decline may be due to changing user expectations. Further user testing may be needed to define objective quality metrics.

test_cases.title: Verify existing users who previously accessed free workouts can access same collection without paywall
preconditions: Existing user account with history of accessing free workouts before subscription paywall introduction.
App updated to latest version containing the fix.
steps: Log in as an existing user with prior free workout history.
Navigate to the workout library.
Attempt to open a workout that was previously accessed for free.
Observe if any paywall or subscription prompt appears.
expected_results: The workout opens and plays without any paywall or subscription prompt.
The user can access the full workout content exactly as before the paywall was introduced.

test_cases.title: Verify no paywall appears for core workout content that was free in previous version
preconditions: App installed, either logged in or logged out.
Identification of core workouts that were free before the subscription paywall introduction (from pre-update snapshot or product documentation).
steps: Open the app and navigate to the workout categories/list.
Identify core workouts that were previously free.
Attempt to start one of those core workouts without a subscription.
expected_results: The core workout starts or plays without requiring a subscription.
No paywall overlay appears; any upsell is non-blocking and does not prevent access to the core workout.

test_cases.title: Verify new users see subscription prompts only for premium features, not for previously free core workouts
preconditions: Fresh installation of the app.
New user account with no prior history.
steps: Sign up as a new user.
Browse workouts and attempt to access a core workout that was previously free.
Observe any prompts.
Attempt to access a premium feature (e.g., personalized training plan).
Observe any prompts.
expected_results: The previously free core workout is accessible without any subscription prompt.
Premium features trigger a subscription prompt as expected.

test_cases.title: Verify purchase screen displays exact price, currency, billing frequency, and trial end date before charge
preconditions: User eligible for free trial or subscription, not yet subscribed.
App has subscription offers configured.
steps: Navigate to the subscription purchase screen.
Review all text and disclosures on the screen.
Note the displayed price, currency, billing frequency, and trial end date.
expected_results: The screen explicitly shows the exact numeric price, currency symbol (e.g., $39.99 USD), billing frequency (e.g., yearly), and exact trial end date and time.
All required billing details are visible before user confirms purchase.

test_cases.title: Verify user can cancel trial/subscription directly from app and receive confirmation
preconditions: User has an active trial or subscription.
User is logged into the app.
steps: Go to account or subscription settings.
Find the cancellation option.
Initiate cancellation and confirm.
Observe the confirmation message and subscription status change.
expected_results: Cancellation is completed within the app without requiring external contact.
User receives a clear confirmation message indicating the subscription is cancelled and no further charges will occur.
Subscription status changes to cancelled immediately.

test_cases.title: Verify no charges occur after user cancels before trial end date
preconditions: User has cancelled trial before end date as per TC-005.
Backend billing system and logs are accessible for verification.
steps: After cancellation, monitor billing events and system logs for any charge attempts at or after the trial end date.
Check for any pending or completed transactions.
expected_results: No billing events occur for the user after cancellation.
System logs show no charge transactions after the cancellation timestamp.
The user is not charged any amount.

test_cases.title: Verify ad overlay includes visible close button that dismisses with one tap
preconditions: App is showing an ad (e.g., before or after a free workout session).
steps: Trigger an ad display.
Observe the ad overlay for a visible close button.
Tap the close button once.
expected_results: The ad overlay dismisses immediately upon tapping close.
User returns to the previous screen or workout.
The close button is clearly visible and clickable.

test_cases.title: Verify no automatic redirects to external websites or app stores after ad display/dismissal
preconditions: App shows ads.
Device is monitored for browser or app store openings.
steps: Trigger an ad.
Allow the ad to complete or close it.
Observe if any external website or app store page opens automatically.
expected_results: No external website or app store page opens without user interaction.
If the ad is closed, no redirect occurs.
If the ad is watched to completion, no auto-redirect occurs.

test_cases.title: Verify no app crash or forced close during ad display or dismissal
preconditions: App running with ads enabled.
Device logs monitored for crashes.
steps: Display 10 consecutive ads.
Attempt to close each ad.
Observe app stability after each ad.
expected_results: App remains stable with no crashes or forced closes.
User can continue using the app normally after each ad dismissal.

test_cases.title: Verify ads do not interrupt active workout sessions unless intentionally triggered
preconditions: User is in an active workout session.
No ad is intentionally triggered by the user (e.g., to unlock content).
steps: Start a workout.
Perform exercises for several minutes without interacting with ad prompts.
Observe if any ad appears unexpectedly.
expected_results: No ad appears during the active workout session.
Ads only appear at expected points (e.g., after workout completion, if applicable) or when user explicitly triggers them.

test_cases.title: Verify original workout library from before AI update is still accessible

A list of original workouts from before the AI update is available for comparison.

Search for specific original workouts.
Attempt to open one original workout.
expected_results: Original workouts are present and playable.
Content matches pre-update versions (e.g., real instructor videos, not AI-generated).

test_cases.title: Verify AI-generated workouts are labeled as AI and are optional additions
preconditions: App has both AI-generated and original content.
steps: Browse the workout list.
Identify AI-generated workouts.
Observe labeling.
Check if any original workout has been replaced by AI content.
expected_results: Each AI-generated workout is clearly labeled as AI.
Original workouts are not replaced; AI content is separate or clearly marked as an alternative.

test_cases.title: Verify user can switch between AI-generated and original content in settings
preconditions: App installed.
User has access to both content types.
steps: Go to settings.
Locate content preference option (e.g., toggle between AI and original).
Switch to 'original' and verify library shows original content.
Switch to 'AI' and verify library shows AI content.
expected_results: Settings include a control to switch between AI-generated and original content.
Changing the setting updates the displayed workout library accordingly.
User can easily switch back and forth.

preconditions: Pre-update baseline metrics for crash-free session rate and workout completion rate are known.
Post-update metrics will be collected over a defined monitoring period.

Record crash-free session rate and workout completion rate.
Compare recorded metrics to pre-update baseline.
expected_results: Crash-free session rate is greater than or equal to baseline.
